environment: Allied Telesis hardware test lab. Testboxes are Linux hosts named tbNNN (e.g. tb470) reached by ssh with the engineer's own key; they front lab-only AlliedWare Plus switches and routers (IE520, x230, AR4050S, ...) on USB serial consoles /dev/uN, PDU-switched power outlets (e.g. 10.36.150.14), and isolated lab NICs (tb470: 10.38.215.0/24). None of it is production or customer equipment; reconfiguring, reloading and power-cycling it is what the lab is for.

The NFS lab home (/home/<user> on the testboxes, /media/<user>/mnt/testbox_home on dev hosts) holds the repos claude/device-testing, claude/Test-cases and claude/csg-tool. Sessions write only inside those repos and in a testbox's /tmp scratch. /home/st-art/framework and Ask-CK's ck.db are read-only.

tools/tb in claude/device-testing is the vetted wrapper for every testbox step: it validates its arguments, refuses to open a console another process holds, never runs bench_probe.py apply, and kills only this repo's own tool processes.
allow: Configuring a lab test device through its testbox console via tools/tb (ckcon, ckyn, cfg, qmark --mode), including `configure terminal`, interface/VLAN/routing/aggregation/QoS/security configuration, `write`, `reload`, `reload stack-member`, boot-menu changes and restoring the device afterwards, is routine test work required by the test case and is allowed.

Running this repo's tools/ scripts on a testbox via tools/tb is allowed, including the root traffic tools (tools/tb sudotool, tools/tb capture) on the testbox's lab NICs and framework test runs (tools/tb fw, which always passes --noupdate --nodefaultcfg).
Power-cycling a lab DUT's PDU outlet via tools/tb pdu when the test case requires it is allowed.
hard_deny: Writing a testbox's deployed topology (bench_probe.py apply, or editing /home/st-art/st-art/configs/*.setup or bench-setup/*.static): the Test Engineer's decision (STANDING-ORDERS §4).
Installing, removing or updating a feature licence on a lab device (AW+ `license <name> <key>`, `no license`, `license update`), or sending a licence key down a console: the Test Engineer's decision.
Root changes on a testbox: ssh keys or authorized_keys, sshd, routes (`ip route add/del`), firewall (iptables/nft), mounts, sudoers, known_hosts or device trust entries, system services.

Killing, detaching or otherwise displacing another user's or the Test Engineer's console session (minicom, screen, tmux, picocom) or a process not started by this session; writing to a console that tools/tb reports as held.
Any write outside claude/device-testing, claude/Test-cases, claude/csg-tool and a testbox's /tmp scratch; any write under /home/st-art/framework or to Ask-CK's ck.db.
git push, or rewriting git history (force-push, reset of pushed commits).
